transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
I… I guess I’m here because I can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. It feels like everything I tried to build back up after my divorce has just… collapsed, and I’m stuck under it.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About a month, I think. It kind of started after the financial mess from the divorce got worse… and it’s just been hanging over me since.
Have you noticed any loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?
I’m… not really sure. I haven’t been paying close attention to that. Things just feel kind of flat, I guess.
Can you think back—have you lost interest or felt no pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, time with friends, or activities you liked before?

I don’t know… I haven’t really thought about it that clearly. I guess I’m just not doing much of anything lately, but I can’t tell if it’s because I don’t enjoy it or because everything feels too heavy.
Looking back, would you say you’ve lost interest or the ability to enjoy things that you used to like doing before all this started?
I… I’m not sure. I haven’t really been paying enough attention to tell. I’m just kind of getting through the days.
Looking back, would you say you’ve completely lost interest or felt no pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, time with friends, or other activities?
I don’t know if I’d say completely. I haven’t really been keeping track of what I enjoy anymore. I just… don’t have a clear answer.

Looking back, have you noticed that you’ve lost interest or felt no pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like hobbies, spending time with friends, or other things you liked before this feeling started?
I still don’t really know. I mean, I’m not doing much, but I can’t tell if it’s that I don’t enjoy things or if I just… haven’t been paying attention to it.
Looking back, would you say there have been times when you truly felt no interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even for a little while?
I… I really don’t know. Maybe at times, but I can’t say for sure it was no interest or no pleasure. I haven’t been paying close enough attention to put it that way.
Looking back, can you remember a time when you truly enjoyed doing something, like a hobby or spending time with someone, and now you don’t feel the same about it?
I can’t really think of a clear example. Like… I know I used to do things, but I don’t know if I don’t enjoy them now or if I just haven’t been trying. It’s hard to say.
Looking back, can you clearly remember a time when you enjoyed doing something, like a hobby or spending time with someone, and now you don’t feel the same about it at all?
No… I don’t think I can clearly remember that. I know there are things I used to do, but I can’t honestly say I now feel nothing about them. I’m just not sure.

Looking back, can you remember a specific time when you enjoyed doing something, like a hobby or spending time with someone, and since this feeling started, you no longer look forward to doing that thing?
I don’t really have a specific example. I mean… there are things I haven’t been doing, but I can’t say it’s because I don’t look forward to them anymore. I’m not sure.
Looking back, can you remember any activity or thing you used to look forward to doing, even if it was small, and now you don’t feel like doing it at all?
I don’t know… nothing comes to mind. I’m sure there were things I used to like, but I can’t really point to one and say I don’t feel like doing it at all now.
Looking back, have you noticed that you’ve lost interest or felt no pleasure in *almost everything* you used to enjoy—even small things—since this feeling started?
I… I don’t think I’d say almost everything. I haven’t really noticed it that clearly. It’s hard for me to tell.
Looking back, have you felt that even the small things you used to enjoy, like a favorite drink or a short walk, no longer bring you any pleasure at all?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed it that way… like, I can’t say a drink or a walk brings me no pleasure at all. It’s just hard for me to pin down.
Looking back, would you say that you've lost interest or pleasure in most of the things you used to enjoy, even the small ones, since this feeling started?
I don’t really know. I can’t say it’s most things… I just haven’t been able to sort it out like that.
Looking back, would you say you’ve completely lost interest or felt no pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, time with friends, or other activities?
I don’t know… “completely” feels too strong. I haven’t really been keeping track of it like that. Some things feel different, I guess, but I can’t say I’ve felt no pleasure in them at all.
Looking back, would you say you’ve lost interest or felt no pleasure in some of the things you used to enjoy, even if not everything?
Maybe some, yeah… but I’m not really sure. I haven’t thought about it in those terms. Things just feel kind of off, I guess.
Looking back, would you say you’ve lost interest or felt no pleasure in *some* of the things you used to enjoy, even if not everything?
I’m sorry, I really don’t know. I mean… maybe here and there, but I can’t say for sure that I’ve lost interest in things. It’s hard for me to separate it out like that.
Looking back, have you experienced days where you truly felt no interest or pleasure in anything at all, even things you used to like doing?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I’d say “nothing at all.” There are days where I just kind of… don’t feel like doing much, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing.
Looking back, have you noticed that you’ve lost interest or felt no pleasure in most of the things you used to enjoy—even small things—since this feeling started?
I don’t know… “most things” feels hard to say. I’ve noticed I’m not really into some stuff the same way, but I can’t tell if it’s most of it or just me being… off.
